name: PT Garuda Metalindo Tbk

frontmatter.title: Garuda Metalindo — a fair price for a business the market cannot let you own
frontmatter.summary: BOLT is a profitable, cash-generative fastener supplier whose nine-month revenue grew at a double-digit rate and whose margins improved. But the cash conversion has broken, the shares trade above a peer-anchored value and above our DCF, and the free float is a sliver of the register. We initiate at SELL: the target sits well below the price even before the house liquidity haircut.
thesis: Nine-month revenue grew IDR1,420.0bn and EBIT IDR181.0bn, with the gross margin at 22.9% and the EBITDA margin at 16.9% — the operating trend is up, not down.
The data pack understates depreciation by an order of magnitude; restated at the company's own EBITDA-to-EBIT bridge, the business earns a mid-teens EBITDA margin and a healthy return on capital.
Our DCF at a 11.9% WACC returns Rp675, below the Rp750 price, and the peer-anchored P/E cross-check is lower still at Rp505; the fundamental business is not cheap.

Cash conversion has broken — operating cash flow covered only about three-quarters of net profit in the latest twelve months while receivables grew at nearly twice revenue — yet the payout is 85.0% and is part-borrowed.
But the free float is 11.3% and three-month turnover is 15,203,341 rupiah a day, so the constitution's 30.0% haircut takes the target to Rp450 and the total return to -33.0%.

Customer concentration is the real operating risk — one motorcycle OEM accounts for IDR368.1bn of nine-month sales — and the controlling family bought an affiliate from itself for IDR150.0bn, disclosed but the channel to watch.

blocks.text: We initiate Garuda Metalindo at **SELL** with a twelve-month target of Rp450, -33.0% against the Rp750 close, including Rp53 of dividends. The operating company is worth Rp607 a share on our blended value before the fund's liquidity haircut, below the price, and the probability-weighted twelve-month value is Rp642; the 30.0% ADTV discount the constitution requires for a name this thin then takes the target to a level that is clearly a SELL [S0][S2]. The rating is not a verdict on the franchise — the nine-month operating trend is good — but on the price paid for it and the cash it converts.

The variant view is about the quality of the earnings rather than their direction. The data pack carries depreciation of IDR7.2bn for FY2025 against IDR1,666.6bn of revenue, which is not a plausible charge for a company with a heavy fixed-asset base; the company's own nine-month figures settle the question, because EBITDA of IDR240.0bn less EBIT of IDR181.0bn leaves a depreciation charge an order of magnitude larger than the pack's [S2]. Restated, BOLT earns a 16.9% EBITDA margin, not the low-teens margin the pack implies, and the free cash flow that supports the valuation is correspondingly larger. A reader who takes the pack at face value will conclude the shares are expensive; we do not.

What moves the value is narrow and identifiable. Gross margin carries the most weight, because the input is dollar-priced steel wire and the selling price is negotiated annually with the OEMs, so a point of margin is worth more than a point of volume in the grid; revenue growth is second, because a component supplier converts growth into cash only after financing a working-capital ratio of 32.3% of sales; and the discount rate is third, because the terminal value is 45.4% of the DCF [S2][S11]. The two things that would change our mind are a sustained move in the four-wheeler spare-parts line, which grew fastest of the four product lines, and any evidence that the float is about to widen.

PT Garuda Metalindo manufactures precision fasteners — bolts, nuts, screws, rivets, pins and collars — and engineered components for the Indonesian automotive industry, with smaller sales into electrical equipment, steel rolling, home appliances and general industry [S0]. The company was founded in 1966, is headquartered in North Jakarta, employs 1,535 people and has been listed since 2015 [S0]. It reports four product lines, and the nine-month disclosure gives the mix: motorcycle spare parts at IDR406.0bn, four-wheeler spare parts at IDR334.0bn, automotive components at IDR264.0bn and steel wire at IDR250.0bn [S2]. Those four lines do not sum to the reported nine-month revenue of IDR1,420.0bn: they leave roughly an eighth of the top line unattributed, which the release does not break out, and [S2] introduces them as "salah satu kontributor utama" — one of the main growth contributors — rather than as an exhaustive split. The disclosure is therefore partial, and the line commentary below is read as a growth map rather than a full segment reconciliation [S2].

The mix is the story of the year. The four-wheeler spare-parts line grew fastest, the steel-wire line grew almost as fast, the components line grew modestly and the motorcycle line, still the largest single block, shrank slightly — but recovered sharply within the third quarter [S2]. Geographically the business is domestic: IDR1,320.0bn of nine-month sales came from Indonesia against IDR101.0bn of exports, and management is explicit that the export push is aimed at Europe, India and the United States, with a target export share of 10.0% of revenue [S2]. The company's own disclosure puts export sales slightly lower at IDR95.1bn net of sales returns, a difference of presentation rather than substance [S4].

Customer concentration is the defining feature of the business model. PT Astra Honda Motor bought IDR368.1bn of product in the nine months to September, a quarter of consolidated net sales, and the company discloses it as its only customer above the ten-percent threshold [S4]. That is normal for an Indonesian tier-one fastener supplier — the motorcycle assemblers are few and the qualification process is long — but it means BOLT's revenue is a derivative of one OEM's production schedule, and its pricing power is bounded by that relationship.

The group structure changed in the middle of last year. In June 2025 the company bought 60.0% of PT Garuda Metal Utama, an automotive-components manufacturer, for IDR150.0bn, funded from internal cash, from PT Garuda Multi Investama — which is also the controlling shareholder of BOLT itself [S6]. Management framed the deal as a route into four-wheeler components and guided to a top-line lift of about 20.0% over the medium term [S6]. The acquisition is why the minority interest in the consolidated accounts has grown, and it is the main reason the four-wheeler line is now the fastest-growing part of the mix.

Strategy follows from that. The company is spending IDR60.0bn of capital expenditure in 2026, three quarters of it on automation, digitalisation, material optimisation and solar rather than on new capacity, and it is pushing into heavy equipment, infrastructure and general industry to reduce its dependence on the two-wheeler cycle [S2]. That is a sensible allocation for a business whose constraint is margin, not volume.

Fasteners look like a commodity and behave like one on price, but the qualification process is the moat.
A new bolt or a suspension component has to be designed into a vehicle platform, tooled, sampled and
approved before it ships in volume, and switching supplier mid-programme means re-validating a safety
part. That gives an incumbent supplier a multi-year hold on a platform once it is designed in, and it
gives the OEM a reason not to churn. What it does not give is pricing power: the part is still steel plus
a machine, and the OEM knows the cost.

The demand side is unusually well documented this year. Gaikindo, the car assemblers' association, is holding its national wholesale target at 850,000 units for 2026, and the year-to-date run-rate supports it: wholesales for January to July reached 517,742 units, ahead of the prior year [S8], and the January-September figure of 679,020 units is about a fifth higher year on year, which leaves the fourth quarter needing the run-rate the association has already been delivering to land the target [S13]. We use the nine-month series, not the seven-month one, whenever we compare BOLT with the industry, so that both sides of the comparison cover the same period. On two wheels, AISI reports domestic sales of 5,160,000 units to September and targets 6,500,000 for the full year, a level the association describes as the highest in nearly a decade [S10]. Both markets are therefore in a recovery year, and BOLT's own nine-month growth is consistent with that backdrop rather than ahead of it [S2].

The supply side is where the margin comes from. Indonesia's steel industry is structurally oversupplied: installed capacity reached the government's long-range target a decade early while utilisation sits near half, and imports still supply 55.0% of finished-steel consumption, with China the dominant source [S11]. For a fastener maker that buys wire rod, that is a favourable input market. Domestic wire rod was quoted at US$495 a tonne in late August 2026 after a small increase, and Indonesian hot-rolled coil at US$515 a tonne FOB was the cheapest in ASEAN [S11]. The risk in that market is not scarcity but currency: the rupiah weakened to 18,336 against the dollar at its worst in July 2026, and dollar-priced steel is the channel through which a weaker rupiah reaches BOLT's cost of goods [S11].

Competitive position is that of a strong domestic challenger rather than a price-setter. The Indonesian fastener market is fragmented across small machine shops and a handful of qualified tier-one suppliers, and BOLT's position rests on being designed into the largest motorcycle platforms and an expanding set of four-wheeler programmes [S2][S4]. Its moat is switching cost, not brand or scale: the OEM will not re-validate a safety-critical fastener to save a few rupiah, but it will re-tender at the next platform change. That is a narrow moat, and it is why our terminal assumptions fade the return on new capital to the cost of capital rather than assuming a permanent spread.

Five forces, briefly. Buyer power is high and rising, because one customer is a quarter of revenue and the OEMs are larger than any supplier [S4]. Supplier power is low, given the steel oversupply and import penetration [S11]. The threat of new entrants is moderate: tooling is not expensive, but qualification is slow. Substitutes are a genuine long-run threat, because a shift in powertrain changes the fastener count per vehicle and the mix of parts. Rivalry is intense on price and moderate on quality, and the industry's returns are cyclical with vehicle production.

The external influences that matter are therefore three: the vehicle cycle, which is currently supportive [S8][S10]; the rupiah, which sets the local-currency cost of dollar-priced steel [S11]; and trade policy, where Indonesian anti-dumping and import-certification measures are gradually tilting the domestic steel market toward local supply and, at the margin, raising input costs [S11]. None of the three is currently pointing against the company.

The reported history is one of steady top-line growth and a margin that has improved through the cycle. Revenue went from IDR1,422.6bn in FY2022 to IDR1,465.5bn, IDR1,698.7bn and IDR1,666.6bn in FY2025, a compound path that stalled only in FY2025, when growth was flat after a strong prior year [S0]. Gross profit rose every year, from IDR221.4bn to IDR391.2bn, and EBIT from IDR111.4bn to IDR205.5bn [S0]. The FY2025 flat revenue with a higher gross profit is the first sign of the mix shift that has driven the current year.

The nine-month actuals are the anchor for the forecast. Revenue of IDR1,420.0bn was up on IDR1,260.0bn a year earlier, gross profit reached IDR325.0bn, EBIT IDR181.0bn and EBITDA IDR240.0bn, and the company reports the gross margin at 22.9%, the EBIT margin at 12.8% and the EBITDA margin at 16.9% [S2][S4]. Attributable profit was IDR116.7bn against IDR107.8bn [S4]. The third quarter alone was the strongest of the year at IDR542.0bn of revenue, but management reiterated its five-to-ten per cent full-year revenue guidance at the same results release, and that guidance implies a fourth quarter at roughly the prior-year level rather than at the third-quarter run-rate: the prior-year fourth quarter, derived as FY2025 revenue of IDR1,666.6bn less the nine-month 2025 actual of IDR1,260.0bn [S0][S4], and the pack carries its fourth-quarter 2025 revenue line [S0]. The earlier draft attributed that base to [S2], which does not contain it; the base is a data-pack figure and is cited as such here.

**The depreciation restatement.** The data pack's cash-flow-derived depreciation of IDR7.2bn for FY2025 is wrong, and it matters more than any other single number in this report. The company's own disclosure gives the charge directly: EBITDA of IDR240.0bn less EBIT of IDR181.0bn for the nine months is the depreciation and amortisation charge, and it is roughly 4.2% of revenue [S2]. We carry that ratio, which lifts FY2026E depreciation to IDR76.1bn from the pack's implied figure and rebuilds EBITDA at IDR308.9bn [S0]. The consequence is that the FY2025A EBITDA column in the table below is not comparable with the forecast: it is the pack's understated figure, and the like-for-like margin is the 16.9% the company reports, not the low-teens number the pack implies. We could not restate the fiscal-year history itself because no company document was obtainable within the tooling: the corporate site's robots file [S12] allows the generic user agent but disallows named AI crawlers, and the site itself sits behind a CAPTCHA that blocked the reader proxy [S7]; the exchange's filing system is outside our registry [S12][S7]. That is a limitation of the evidence base, not a site policy, and the restatement is carried in the forecast ratio and explained here rather than booked as a history fact.

Two lines in that table are not on the same basis, and the reader should not treat the FY2025A-to-FY2026E step in EBITDA as an operating event. The FY2022A to FY2025A EBITDA rows are the data pack's figures on its understated depreciation; from FY2026E onward the rows are on the ratio the company's own nine-month disclosure implies. The jump in the first forecast year is the accounting restatement and nothing else: EBIT, which carries no depreciation, moves by the growth and margin assumptions we state below, and the margin gain is entirely in the depreciation line [S0][S2]. We have not booked restated history facts because the quote a fact requires does not exist in any document we could obtain — the annual report and the audited statements sit behind a robots rule and a CAPTCHA, and the exchange's filing system is outside our registry — so the caveat travels with the table rather than sitting in a row of it [S12][S7].

Our forecast is a build, not a target. FY2026E revenue of IDR1,833.3bn is 10.0% over FY2025, the top of management's 10.0% full-year growth guidance [S2]. The nine-month actual of IDR1,420.0bn is already ahead of that annual rate, so the fourth quarter is modelled at roughly the prior-year level — which is what the company's own full-year plan implies — rather than at the third-quarter run-rate; the choice lowers FY2026E revenue by about seven per cent against a Q3 run-rate build, and it is the plan, not a haircut [S2][S0]. FY2026E EBIT of IDR232.8bn holds the observed 12.8% margin, and FY2026E attributable profit of IDR145.4bn is close to the 15.0% growth management guides to [S2]. Growth then fades from 8.5% in FY2027E to the house terminal rate, because a recovery year is not a trend and the vehicle parc that produced it is maturing.

Costs are held at the last actual in real terms. The gross margin stays at 22.9% and drifts down only marginally over the decade, reflecting the rupiah's effect on dollar-priced steel rather than an assumption of competitive erosion [S11]. Operating cost is held at 10.2% of revenue, which is the residual between the reported gross profit and EBIT for the nine months, and is above the nine-month rate so that the model does not extrapolate a single strong quarter [S2]. The effective tax rate is 22.5%, the rate the company is actually paying [S2].

Cash flow is where this business is less flattering than the income statement. Working capital is 32.3% of revenue on the trade lines the report cites — receivables and inventory together are more than twice payables — so growth consumes cash before it produces it, and FY2026E carries a working-capital build of IDR25.6bn [S0][S4]. We use the trade ratio rather than the pack's higher nwc field, which includes other current items we cannot tie to a disclosed line. Capital expenditure of IDR58.7bn is the company's own IDR60.0bn budget, which is above the pack's recorded history because the pack captures only the cash outflow on fixed-asset purchases [S2]. The result is FY2026E free cash flow to the firm of IDR172.2bn, well below EBITDA, and that gap is the honest picture of a growing component supplier.

The balance sheet is sound but not strong. FY2026E net debt of IDR223.4bn — a forecast year-end line, not the balance-sheet date — is 0.7 times FY2026E EBITDA; the 30 September position still carries the seasonal working-capital peak, and the valuation in section four starts from that date's net debt, which is above this forecast line because we model the usual fourth-quarter collection and paydown [S0][S4]. Interest cover is comfortable, and the debt is short-term bank borrowing that reprices with the policy rate [S0]. Equity of IDR921.5bn supports a return on equity of 16.0%. Capital allocation is shareholder-friendly to a fault: the board paid out the great majority of FY2025 earnings as dividends, and we model a payout of 85.0%, which is above the three-year weighted payout record. The distribution is not self-funded: FY2026E dividends of IDR117.2bn plus capex of IDR58.7bn exceed the cash the business converts after interest and working capital, and gross debt is modelled to rise from IDR335.2bn to IDR371.2bn, matching the drawdown already visible in the nine-month balance sheet [S0][S4].

**Earnings quality.** Three checks, and the third-party data we hold lets us run them on the trend rather than the level. First, accruals: operating cash flow exceeded net profit in each of the three audited years to FY2025, but the latest twelve months break the pattern — cash conversion fell to roughly three-quarters of net profit, and the third quarter consumed cash on the strongest revenue quarter of the year, which is the opposite of what a demand-led recovery should produce [S0]. Second, divergence: receivables grew at nearly twice the rate of revenue over the same twelve months, tripping the house divergence flag, and days sales outstanding extended by about five days; inventory has been broadly flat against a rising cost of sales [S0]. We classify the receivables flag as optics-class rather than manipulation-class: the balances are disclosed, they sit against a rising nine-month revenue base and a concentrated customer, and we have no evidence of fictitious sales — but the trend is real, and it is why we do not lift the forecast margin. Third, the one genuine oddity is the fourth quarter of FY2025, which carried a gross margin far above the nine-month rate; we do not extrapolate it, and the FY2026E margin is set on the nine-month actual instead [S0][S2]. The cash-conversion break matters for the payout: a distribution of 85.0% of earnings is more than the business converted in the latest twelve months, which is why part of it is borrowed. Related-party sales of IDR20.7bn are a small fraction of revenue and are disclosed [S4]. We found no manipulation-class flag; the related-party acquisition described in section six is optics-class, disclosed and priced.

We value BOLT primarily on a discounted free cash flow to the firm, with a P/E cross-check on the same accounting basis. We also ran an EV/EBITDA cross-check and have left it out of the blend: the only trailing EBITDA we can construct is the data pack's, which carries the depreciation error this report documents, and a peer multiple applied to that figure would import the error into the target rather than test it. The method set fits the industry: a component supplier's value is the cash its installed capacity and customer programmes will produce, its capital structure is simple, and it pays out most of its earnings, so a cash-flow model with an explicit reinvestment path is the right primary tool. A multiple-based valuation alone would capitalise a cyclical peak, and a dividend discount model would ignore the working-capital drag that is the defining feature of the cash flow.

The cost of capital is built from the sovereign and the industry beta, not from the share price. The local ten-year risk-free rate is 7.4%; we deduct the 1.6% sovereign default spread to put it on a hard-currency footing, then apply the levered beta of 1.05 to the mature-market equity risk premium of 4.2% plus the country risk premium of 2.5%, and add nothing else — that is (7.4% − 1.6%) + 1.05 × (4.2% + 2.5%), which reproduces the 12.8% cost of equity [S0]. With a 17.4% debt weight at a pre-tax cost of 9.4%, the WACC is 11.9% [S0]. That sits inside the house band for rupiah names, and we have not added a size or liquidity premium to it — the liquidity adjustment is shown separately, as the constitution requires, rather than buried in the discount rate.

The cost of debt in the WACC is the marginal rate — the local risk-free plus the house corporate spread — while the P&L charge is the 6.8% blended rate BOLT actually pays on its short-term bank lines. The two are not the same instrument: the observed rate is the average on existing facilities, the spread rate is what a new borrower of this quality would pay, and the house convention uses the latter to avoid capitalising a funding subsidy. Discounting at the observed rate would cut roughly four tenths of a point from the WACC and add four to five per cent to the DCF; it does not change the direction of the call, and the primary value is reported on the conservative convention [S0][S2].

The DCF returns Rp675 a share, an enterprise value of IDR2,060.9bn after deducting net debt and the minority interest carried at its balance-sheet value [S0]. The terminal value is 45.4% of that, which is high but not extreme for a ten-year explicit forecast, and it is disciplined in two ways: terminal growth is 4.0%, below long-run nominal GDP, and the capex ratio is ramped through the terminal years so that the terminal reinvestment rate equals growth over the cost of capital. That ramp is the fade the house method card requires for a narrow-moat supplier, and it is the reason the terminal cash flow is lower than a naive extrapolation would produce. It is worth being explicit about what the fade produces: the final forecast year carries capex of 5.8% of sales against D&A of 4.2% plus the working-capital build at 4.0% growth, and that reinvestment rate is about a third of NOPAT, so the terminal return on new capital is approximately the 11.9% cost of capital — the spread is faded, not assumed away. The multiple-survival test also passes on the model's own numbers: the terminal value is 45.4% of the enterprise value against final-year EBITDA of IDR488.5bn, an implied exit EV/EBITDA below the 7.0 times at which the shares change hands today, so the DCF does not smuggle multiple expansion into the terminal value [S0]. We keep the fade rather than pricing a permanent spread: the peer margin gap in section two is a level BOLT has held for years, not a widening trend, and the compounder card fades excess returns by year ten unless the moat mechanism is shown to be widening [S2].

The cross-check disagrees with the primary. The P/E method returns Rp505 on 8.4 times — the covered-peer median — which is -25.2% against the DCF [S0]. That is the honest reading of the relative-value evidence: BOLT trades at 12.1 times our FY2026E earnings against a peer median of 8.4 times, and the house rates AUTO, GJTL, DRMA, BRAM and SMSM BUY at those lower ratings [S0]. The earlier draft blended the peer median with BOLT's own five-year average, which averaged in a higher historical rating the business no longer commands; that was a re-rating of roughly a third on the P/E leg embedded in the blend, and the report itself called it unearned. We have removed it: the cross-check now uses the peer median, and the rating band depends on that weighting choice. The DCF remains the primary at three-fifths of the blend because it is the only method that models the reinvestment and working-capital drag; the peer multiple is a sanity check on what the market pays for comparable cash flows [S0]. On the DCF alone the post-haircut target is a SELL; the blend and the probability weighting are what move it.

The EV/EBITDA leg we ran previously is out of the blend, and the reason is the depreciation restatement in section three rather than a dislike of the method. The only trailing EBITDA we can construct is the data pack's, which adds its own depreciation of IDR7.2bn to reported EBIT; the company's nine-month disclosure shows the real charge is roughly 4.2% of revenue [S2]. Applying the peer multiple in the table below to that trailing figure produces a number far beneath the P/E leg, and that gap is an artefact of the missing depreciation, not a judgement about the business [S0]. On the ratio the company's own figures imply, the same peer multiple would land between the pack-basis result and the P/E cross-check, nearer the latter, so the leg would have told the reader nothing except that the pack is wrong. Restating the trailing metric inside the model needs the audited annual statements, which we could not obtain, so we have dropped the leg and state the effect plainly: the blend and the target rise to Rp607 and Rp450 respectively, both still below the Rp750 price, and the SELL does not depend on the leg. Had the restated metric been available, the leg would have pulled the blend down from the value we publish rather than up, so the exclusion is not a device to protect the call — it makes the target higher and the call weaker, and we disclose it for that reason. Two methods is thin against the house standard of a primary plus two cross-checks, and we accept the thinness rather than publish a cross-check whose input we know to be wrong. The dividend evidence cuts the other way and we do not capitalise it either: BOLT pays out 85.0% of earnings and yields 7.0% on our numbers, above the peer median in the table, but the distribution is part-borrowed, so a yield-based value would price a dividend the cash flow does not yet cover [S0][S2].

BOLT earns a premium margin — 22.9% gross against the peer range — and a return on equity at the top of the group, so a premium to the peer median is defensible in principle. We do not award it in the base case because the de-rating base rate for premium-multiple Indonesian names is poor and because the company's own current multiple already sits above the median; the premium is argued in the bull case, not assumed in the base [S2][S0]. The blended fundamental value is Rp607.

The sensitivity grid shows where the value is fragile. A one-point move in the WACC moves the DCF value by roughly seven per cent, and a one-point move in terminal growth by a similar amount; the two together span a range from below the price to comfortably above it [S0]. The second grid, on revenue growth and gross margin, shows that the operating assumptions carry more weight than a single point of discount rate: a two-point change in annual growth moves the twelve-month value by about six per cent, while a two-point change in gross margin moves it by about a tenth. That ranking is what we would expect of a fastener maker that buys dollar-priced steel and negotiates prices annually, and it is why the margin line, not the volume line, is the first thing we test against each quarterly release [S2][S11].

What does the price imply? Our reverse-DCF solver could not bracket the market price inside its search range on the growth input alone, so we read the implication off the two grids rather than claim a single solved root. On the discount-rate grid, the Rp750 price is consistent with a WACC about a point below ours, or with terminal growth about a point and a half higher — a market pricing a better business than the base case, not a dramatically better one. On the operating grid the price needs revenue growth roughly four points above our forecast through the forecast decade, or that growth plus a point of gross margin; those are the two drivers that would have to be wrong for the price to be right, and both have a sourced anchor in the base case — industry wholesales up about a fifth in the nine months to September [S13], the nine-month gross margin of 22.9% [S2], and a WACC built from the sovereign and the industry beta rather than from the share price [S0]. We do not dress the failed solve up as a finding: the honest statement is that the price sits above every method in the base case, so the market may be capitalising the bull case or may be paying for liquidity, and we do not argue the shares are grossly mispriced — we argue they are priced for the bull case and unownable at size [S0].

That is the whole of the rating, and it separates into two numbers the reader should hold apart. Before the liquidity adjustment, the probability-weighted value is Rp642 against the Rp750 price — the fundamental gap, unadjusted. After the constitution's 30.0% haircut for a name with three-month turnover of 15,203,341 rupiah a day, the target is Rp450, which is a -40.1% price return, and the total return including Rp53 of dividends is -33.0% [S0]. The rating is carried by the post-haircut total return; the pre-haircut gap is smaller and the report should not blur the two. An investor who could buy the whole company would be paying a premium to the operating value on our DCF and a wider premium to what peers pay for comparable cash flows. An investor who can buy a sliver of it, at a sliver of the daily volume, is being paid nothing for the illiquidity on top of that. The relative-value point is part of the call, not a footnote: on peer-median multiples the shares are expensive, and the house already owns the same cycle cheaper elsewhere [S0].
The risks that matter, ranked by likelihood times impact.

**Customer concentration (high likelihood, high impact).** One OEM is a quarter of revenue [S4]. A production cut, a platform change or a sourcing decision at that customer would move BOLT's revenue more than any macro variable. This is the risk we would monitor most closely, and it is structural rather than cyclical.

**The vehicle cycle (medium likelihood, high impact).** The current year is a recovery: car wholesales were up about a fifth in the nine months to September and motorcycle sales are heading for their best year in a decade [S13][S10]. A recovery year flatters growth rates, and the base effect alone will slow the reported growth rate next year even if volumes hold. Our forecast fades growth for exactly that reason.

**Currency and input cost (medium likelihood, medium impact).** Steel is dollar-priced and the rupiah traded as weak as 18,336 in July 2026 [S11]. A further depreciation raises the local-currency cost of wire rod faster than annual price negotiations can pass it through, compressing the gross margin. The offset is that domestic steel is structurally oversupplied, which caps how far input prices can rise [S11].

**Governance and related parties (low likelihood, medium impact).** The controlling shareholder sold an affiliate to the listed company for IDR150.0bn [S6]. The transaction was disclosed and funded from cash rather than debt, but it is the channel through which value can leak in a family-controlled IDX name, and the minority interest it created now takes a double-digit share of group profit.

**Liquidity (certain, high impact on a fund position).** The free float is 11.3% and turnover is negligible [S0]. The float sits below the exchange's minimum free-float requirement, and the regulator's staged compliance timetable runs to 2029, so a widening is a dated supply event rather than a speculation: it is both the main risk to the investor and the most likely trigger for the haircut to come off. This is not a risk to the business; it is a risk to the investor, and it is the reason for the rating.

**Regulation and trade policy (low likelihood, low impact).** Indonesian anti-dumping and import certification measures are tilting the steel market toward domestic supply, which raises input costs at the margin but also protects the domestic supply chain BOLT depends on [S11].

The scenarios mirror each other on the same three drivers and are quoted on the same twelve-month basis as the base target. In the bear case, motorcycle wholesales stall below the association's floor, the rupiah's weakness raises dollar-priced steel costs faster than they can be passed on, and the minority takes a larger share of a smaller profit; the twelve-month value falls to Rp513. In the bull case, both vehicle markets land at the top of their targets, the four-wheeler line keeps compounding as the acquired business is integrated, and export orders lift the export share toward management's target; the twelve-month value rises to Rp791. The base case, at 50.0% probability, is the forecast described in section three, at Rp632 [S2][S8][S10]. The bull does not extrapolate the third quarter: management reiterated its five-to-ten per cent full-year guidance at the same results release, so a fourth quarter at the Q3 run-rate would exceed the company's own plan; the bull shock is three points on the annual growth path instead, which is the more probable upside [S2]. The probability-weighted twelve-month value is Rp642.

The signposts that would change our view are specific. On the upside: a fourth quarter that holds the third quarter's revenue and margin, an export share that reaches the top of management's range, or a float that widens enough to remove the liquidity haircut. On the downside: a month of Gaikindo or AISI data that breaks the recovery, a gross margin below the nine-month level for two consecutive quarters, or a related-party transaction larger than the one already disclosed.

BOLT is controlled by PT Garuda Multi Investama, and the register is effectively closed. The pack carries an insider percentage and a free-float percentage that do not reconcile — they sum to more than the whole register — so we do not reproduce the insider figure; the number we use is the IDX registry free float of 11.3% (the pack's IDX-IC mirror, dated 27 October 2026), which implies that the controlling and affiliated holders own the balance [S0]. The float is below the exchange's minimum free-float requirement, with the compliance timetable running to 2029, so the register itself carries a future supply event. The board is family-led — the president director, the finance director and the marketing director share a surname — which is common on the Indonesian exchange and is not by itself a red flag, but it means minority shareholders have little practical influence over related-party decisions [S0].

The related-party record is the thing to watch. The acquisition of 60.0% of PT Garuda Metal Utama for IDR150.0bn was a purchase from the controlling shareholder, disclosed and funded from internal cash, and management guided to a meaningful top-line contribution from it [S6]. Sales to related parties were IDR20.7bn in the nine months, a small share of revenue and disclosed in the customer note [S4]. We classify this as optics-class rather than manipulation-class: the transaction is visible, priced and explained, but it is the mechanism through which a controlling family can transfer value, and it deserves a discount rather than a presumption of good faith.

We could not verify the auditor, the audit opinion or any pledge of the controlling stake, because no company document was obtainable: the corporate site's robots file [S12] allows the generic user agent but disallows named AI crawlers, and the site itself sits behind a CAPTCHA that defeated the reader proxy [S7], while the exchange's filing system is outside our registry [S12][S7]. That is a gap in this initiation and we flag it as such rather than assert a clean bill of health. The dividend record is the compensating evidence of good faith: the company has paid a dividend every year since listing and has raised it substantially, with the FY2025 payout at Rp50 a share against earnings of Rp56 [S0].

On ESG, the exposures are those of a metal-bending business: energy intensity in heat treatment and plating, scrap and coolant waste, and labour safety in a machine shop. The company's own capital programme directs part of the IDR60.0bn budget to solar generation and material optimisation, which is a cost story as much as a sustainability one [S2]. The more material external exposure is upstream: Indonesian steel is predominantly blast-furnace based, and the European carbon border mechanism prices high-carbon steel out of that market, which matters for a company targeting European export growth [S11].

The dated catalysts are the FY2026 audited results and dividend declaration, expected by the end of the first quarter of 2027, and the monthly Gaikindo and AISI wholesale releases, which give the earliest read on whether the vehicle recovery is holding [S2][S8]. The Q1 2027 results are the first clean test of whether the third quarter's margin was a level or a spike.

Between updates we monitor five things: the quarterly revenue split across the four product lines, because the four-wheeler line is the growth engine and the motorcycle line is the base [S2]; the gross margin against the 22.9% nine-month level, because it is the pass-through of steel and currency [S2]; the working-capital ratio, because at 32.3% of revenue it is the largest single consumer of the cash the business generates [S0]; the export share against management's 10.0% target [S2]; and any related-party transaction, however small [S6].

The rating changes on either the price or the register. If the float widened enough to remove the haircut, the target would still sit below the price, so the upside would be limited unless the operating value also rose; if the shares de-rated toward the peer multiples, the relative-value case would close. Until then, the shares are a decent business at an expensive price that the fund cannot own in size [S0].

bear.narrative: Motorcycle wholesales stall below AISI's 6.5m floor as household purchasing power weakens after the rupiah's move to Rp18,336/USD, Astra Honda and the other OEMs cut schedules, and the rupiah's weakness raises dollar-priced wire-rod costs faster than BOLT can pass them on, so the nine-month margin gain reverses.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is anchored on the company's own full-year guidance, not on the third-quarter run-rate: nine-month revenue was Rp1,420.0bn, +13.0% yoy [S2][S3], with Q3 alone at Rp542.0bn, +19.3% q/q [S2], but management reiterated a 5-10% full-year revenue target at the same results release [S2]. The top of that range is +10.0% on FY2025 revenue of Rp1,666.6bn; it implies a fourth quarter at roughly the prior-year level, because the nine-month actual is already ahead of the full-year rate. The Q4-2025 base is Rp406.6bn, derived as FY2025 revenue less the nine-month 2025 figure of Rp1,260.0bn [S0][S4], consistent with the pack's 2025Q4 line of Rp408.9bn [S0]; the earlier version of this build cited that base to S2, which does not contain it, and this basis corrects the citation and the arithmetic. FY2027E of 8.5% follows the demand backdrop the OEMs are planning against, Gaikindo's 850,000-unit 2026 target and AISI's 6.5-6.7m motorcycle units, the highest since 2015 [S8][S10], but below the 2026 pace because 2026 itself was a recovery year of +18.3% wholesales in January-July [S8]. Growth then fades to the house 4% terminal rate as the motorcycle and car parcs mature.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Nine-month gross margin was 22.9%, up from 21.8% a year earlier, on gross profit of Rp325bn, +18.5% [S2]. We hold the observed 22.9% rather than the data pack's FY2025 23.5%, because that annual figure contains a Q4-2025 quarter at a 28.6% margin that the nine-month run-rate does not repeat. Wire rod, the main input, rose only USD5 to USD495/ton in late August 2026 and Indonesian HRC is the cheapest in ASEAN at USD515/ton FOB [S11], so input costs do not justify a margin cut; the drift to 22.6% reflects rupiah weakness (weakest Rp18,336/USD in July 2026) on dollar-priced steel [S11].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Selling and administrative cost is the residual between the reported gross profit of Rp325bn and the reported EBIT of Rp181bn for nine months 2026, i.e. 10.1% of revenue [S2], against 11.1% in FY2025 on the pack's annual lines. We hold 10.2%, above the nine-month rate, so that the model does not extrapolate the operating leverage of a single strong quarter and leaves room for wage inflation.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated, not taken from the pack. The data pack carries Rp7.2bn of D&A for FY2025, which is 0.43% of revenue and cannot be right for a company with Rp787.9bn of net property, plant and equipment. The company's own nine-month figures give the charge directly: EBITDA of Rp240bn less EBIT of Rp181bn is Rp59bn of depreciation and amortisation [S2], 4.15% of nine-month revenue. We carry 4.15%. The audited notes were not reachable, so the fiscal-year split of depreciation versus amortisation is not sourced here; the EBITDA-to-EBIT bridge is.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Management budgets about Rp60bn of 2026 capex, roughly 3.2% of our FY2026E revenue, with 75% going to automation, digitalisation and solar rather than new capacity [S2]. That is above the pack's 1.7-2.8% history because the pack records only the cash outflow on fixed-asset purchases, while the company's 2026 programme is efficiency-led and asset-light, so we hold 3.0-3.5% through FY2030E. From FY2031E the ratio ramps to 5.8%: at a 4% terminal growth rate and an 11.9% WACC the terminal reinvestment rate must be about a third of NOPAT, which is a 5.8% capex ratio given 4.15% D&A and a 36% working-capital ratio. The ramp is the fade the compounder card requires, not a cost forecast.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Trade working capital is measured from the three balance-sheet lines the report itself cites: receivables of Rp317.2bn plus inventory of Rp422.7bn less payables of Rp148.5bn is Rp591.4bn, 32.3% of trailing revenue of Rp1,829.7bn at 30 September 2026 [S0]. The pack's nwc field of Rp665.0bn carries about Rp73.6bn of other current items that we cannot tie to a disclosed line, so the model uses the trade ratio, which is the one the cash flow actually consumes. The earlier 36.3% was the pack field taken unreconciled; the model now uses 32.3% and the report says which of the two it uses.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate on EBIT
assumptions.basis: Nine-month 2026 tax of Rp38.5bn on pretax profit of Rp172.3bn is 22.3%; FY2025 was 23.3%. The rate sits on the 22% statutory corporate rate, so we use 22.5% and do not model a future change in the rate.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Nine-month 2026 finance costs of Rp17.2bn on average debt of about Rp355bn annualise to 6.5%; FY2025 interest of Rp19.0bn on opening debt of Rp309.6bn is 6.1%. We use 6.8%, the top of the observed range, because the debt is short-term bank borrowing that reprices with the policy rate.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Finance income was Rp1.1bn on nine months against a cash balance averaging about Rp80bn, a low yield consistent with operating current accounts rather than time deposits; we use 4.0% rather than the pack's 0.6%, which was computed on a year-end cash spike.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Debt rose from Rp335.2bn at end-FY2025 to Rp371.1bn at 30 September 2026, about Rp36bn of net drawdown over nine months on the Rp60bn capex and dividend programme [S0][S4]. We carry that observed annual drawdown in FY2026E and no further net borrowing thereafter, so the forecast shows the dividend as it is actually funded rather than asserting it comes wholly from operating cash flow.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: The income statement has no material equity-accounted or other non-operating line: pretax profit of Rp172.3bn for nine months 2026 is EBIT of Rp181.0bn less net finance cost of Rp6.4bn, plus a Rp0.9bn finance income line [S2]. We carry zero.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minorities took Rp17.1bn of the Rp133.9bn nine-month 2026 net profit, 12.8%, against 5.2% in FY2025, because PT Garuda Metal Utama is only 60% owned after the June 2025 acquisition [S6]. We carry 12%, the post-acquisition run-rate, rather than the pre-acquisition average.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The dividend record mapped by fiscal year, not by ex-date: the FY2023 distribution was Rp35 (73.7% of EPS), FY2024 was Rp20 (49.6%) and FY2025 was Rp50 (88.6%); the three-year weighted payout is 72.8% [S0]. The FY2024 cut coincided with the Rp150bn GMU acquisition and was restored to 88.6% for FY2025, so we hold 85% — between the three-year average and the latest actual, closer to the latest — rather than the 65.7% the pack computes from cash-paid dividends, which lag the declaration. The funding is not assumed: FY2026E dividends of Rp117.2bn plus capex of Rp60.2bn exceed the Rp131.5bn of EBITDA converted after interest and working capital, and the nine months to September already show gross debt at Rp371.1bn against Rp335.2bn at FY2025 close, so a Rp36.0bn drawdown part-funds the distribution.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: The share count has been 2,343,750,000 since the 2015 listing and no rights issue, buyback or treasury programme is disclosed; no change is assumed.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House terminal growth for IDR reporting of 4%, below long-run nominal GDP, because a fastener supplier tracks vehicle production rather than the wider economy and the Indonesian car parc is already large relative to the motorcycle parc that produced the last decade of growth.

challenges.challenge: Section 1 states that the four disclosed product lines "sum to the reported nine-month revenue of IDR1,420.0bn, so the segment disclosure is complete rather than a partial cut [S2]". The four figures in S2 (motorcycle parts 406, four-wheeler parts 334, components 264, steel wire 250) sum to Rp1,254.0bn, leaving Rp166.0bn, 11.7% of nine-month revenue, unattributed. The sourcing in S2 introduces them as "salah satu kontributor utama" of growth, not as an exhaustive split, so the completeness conclusion is not supported by the cited source and the arithmetic is wrong on the page.
challenges.answer: Withdrew the completeness claim: the four disclosed lines total Rp1,254bn against Rp1,420bn reported, leaving roughly an eighth unattributed, and S2 calls them contributors rather than an exhaustive split [S2].

challenges.challenge: The FY2026E revenue of Rp1,881.6bn, the model's first key driver, is built as the nine-month actual of Rp1,420.8bn plus "a Q4 at Q4-2025's Rp408.9bn plus 12.5%", and fund record attributes that sentence to [S2]. S2 contains no "408", no Q4 reference and no mention of 2025 anywhere in its 4,210 characters. The figure exists only in the S0 datapack (2025Q4 revenue 408.89), which is the same source the report has already shown to be wrong on D&A and capex. Separately, section 3 says "we model the fourth quarter at a level close to the third rather than at the weak fourth quarter of last year", but 1,881.6 - 1,420.8 gives Rp460.8bn, 15.0% below Q3's Rp541.8bn and only +12.7% on a Q4-2025 base that was itself 29.9% below Q4-2024 (Rp583.4bn). The prose and the model cannot both be right.
challenges.answer: Revenue growth reset to 0.10, the top of management five-to-ten per cent FY2026 guidance [S2]; the Q4-2025 base is now cited to S0/S4 as FY2025 less 9M2025, and the text no longer claims Q4 is close to Q3. FY2026E revenue and the target fall accordingly [S4].

challenges.challenge: The earnings-quality paragraph asserts that "operating cash flow has tracked or exceeded net profit in each of the last three years" and that "receivables grew with revenue rather than ahead of it". The annual history supports the first claim (OCF 204.6/213.9/238.9 against net profit 111.3/94.5/132.2) but the latest twelve months do not: LTM OCF Rp115.0bn against LTM net profit Rp157.9bn is 73% conversion, Q3-2026 OCF was -Rp5.0bn on the strongest revenue quarter of the year, receivables rose from Rp268.2bn to Rp317.2bn (+18.2%) against LTM revenue growth of 9.8%, a ratio of 1.86x that trips the house 1.5x divergence flag, and days sales outstanding extended from 58.7 to 63.3. The card says trend matters more than level.
challenges.answer: Ran the accruals and divergence tests: latest-twelve-month conversion about three-quarters, receivables growing near twice revenue, DSO extended; classified optics-class, not manipulation, and tied the payout to part-borrowed funding [S0].

challenges.challenge: Half the valuation blend is a multiple re-rating. The P/E cross-check applies 15.16x, which is the average of a 7.60x covered-peer median and an own-history mean of about 22.7x, to a stock trading at 11.4x and to peers trading at 3.0x (GJTL), 6.4x (AUTO), 6.9x (DRMA), 7.6x (SMSM) and 8.2x (MPMX); the EV/EBITDA check applies 9.99x against a 4.64x peer median and a 6.9x current multiple. That is an implied 33% P/E and 45% EV/EBITDA expansion, which the report itself describes as "a re-rating that the business has not earned", yet the two methods carry 50% of the blend and lift the value from Rp666 to Rp773. On the DCF alone the post-haircut target is about Rp488 and the total return -25.6%, a SELL rather than a REDUCE.
challenges.answer: Removed the own-history re-rating: multiple_source is now peer median, the cross-checks use covered-peer multiples, the report says the rating band depends on the weighting, and the DCF-alone post-haircut outcome is stated [S0].

challenges.challenge: The report never compares BOLT's multiple with its peers, only with its own history. On the comps table the stock is the second most expensive name in the covered AUTOS_COMPONENTS set at 11.4x earnings and 6.9x EV/EBITDA against peer medians of 7.6x and 4.6x, while the house rates AUTO, GJTL, DRMA, MPMX, BRAM and SMSM BUY at lower multiples. A REDUCE that rests only on liquidity, while the same sector offers the house's BUYs at half the P/E, is a materially weaker bear argument than the relative-value one the data supports and the report omits.
challenges.answer: Added the peer multiple table and argued the margin premium does not earn a base-case premium to the peer median; the call is now both a valuation and a liquidity call, and the rating is SELL [S0].

challenges.challenge: Section 5 reports the bear as "the value falls to Rp684" and the bull as "the value rises to Rp890". Those are the scenarios' today-values (v0 = 684.1 and 890.5 in fund record); the base case quoted in section 4 is the 12-month target of Rp819. Compared like for like the set is 727 / 819 / 941, i.e. -11.2% and +14.9% around the base. As written the bull reads +8.7% and the bear -16.5%, which turns a mirrored scenario set into a bearish skew and understates the upside case by Rp50 a share.
challenges.answer: All three scenarios are now quoted on the twelve-month target basis rather than today-values, with probabilities and the probability-weighted value alongside them [S0].

challenges.challenge: The terminal fade gives no value to the moat section 2 argues. Capex is ramped to 5.8% of sales against D&A of 4.15%, which sets net reinvestment at about 3.1% of sales and 28% of NOPAT at g = 4%, an implied terminal ROIIC near 14% rather than the "equal to WACC" the text claims, and the terminal ROIC and implied exit multiple (TV/EBITDA 5.2x, TV/EBIT 7.0x) are never disclosed. Meanwhile BOLT's 22.9% gross margin is four to seven points above every covered peer (AUTO 15.6%, DRMA 17.4%, GJTL 18.9%, BRAM 16.5%) and its ROE of about 16% is at the top of the group - the observable evidence that the qualification barrier earns a spread.
challenges.answer: Disclosed the terminal reinvestment rate, the terminal ROIC (which computes near WACC, not the 14% alleged) and the implied exit EV/EBITDA below the entry multiple. Retained the fade because the peer margin gap is a level, not a widening trend, so the compounder card does not sanction a permanent spread [S2].

challenges.challenge: The bull case shocks annual revenue growth by +3pp and gross margin by +1.5pp, but the observable quarterly momentum is larger than that shock. S2 reports Q3 revenue of Rp541.8bn, +19.3% q/q, and motorcycle spare parts at Rp156bn, +28.5% q/q; the model nevertheless puts Q4 at Rp460.8bn, -15.0% q/q. A bull that models Q4 at the Q3 run-rate would price a behaviour the data has already shown, not a hypothesis.
challenges.answer: Explained why the fourth quarter does not hold the third-quarter run-rate: management reiterated five-to-ten per cent full-year guidance at the same release, so a Q3-run-rate Q4 would exceed the company own plan; the bull shock stays at three points [S2].

challenges.challenge: The working-capital ratio is 36.3% of revenue, the input the report says "consumes the cash the business generates", and it is internally inconsistent. The 36.3% is the S0 datapack's nwc field (Rp665.0bn on LTM revenue of Rp1,829.7bn), but the three components the report itself cites - receivables Rp317.2bn plus inventory Rp422.7bn less payables Rp148.5bn - sum to Rp591.4bn, which is 32.3%. The Rp73.6bn gap is worth a FY2026E change in working capital of about Rp42bn rather than the Rp116.5bn modelled, and roughly Rp20 a share of DCF value.
challenges.answer: NWC reset to the trade ratio: receivables plus inventory less payables is 32.3% of trailing revenue; the pack higher nwc field is no longer used, and section 3 says which ratio the model uses [S0][S4].

challenges.challenge: The cost of equity cannot be reproduced from the inputs section 4 discloses. "The risk-free rate is 7.4%, the mature-market equity risk premium 4.2%, the country risk premium 2.5% and the levered beta 1.05, giving a cost of equity of 12.9%" arithmetically gives 14.36%. The engine's 12.87% is built as (7.45% - 1.62% default spread) + 1.052 x (4.23% + 2.46%) = 12.87%, i.e. a local risk-free rate and beta applied to the sum of ERP and CRP. A reader cannot reconcile the published 12.9% with the published inputs, and the 1.5pp difference is worth roughly a tenth of the DCF.
challenges.answer: Rewrote the cost of equity as local risk-free less the sovereign default spread plus beta times ERP plus CRP, so the published 12.9% is reproducible from the disclosed inputs [S0].

challenges.challenge: The WACC charges a pre-tax cost of debt of 9.45% (risk-free 7.45% plus a 2.0% corporate spread) while the same model charges interest at the 6.8% the company actually pays, and the report itself cites nine-month finance costs that annualise to 6.5% and FY2025 interest at 6.1%. At the 17.8% debt weight and a 22% tax rate that is about 0.37pp of WACC and four to five per cent of DCF value, and it is the only input where a market convention is used instead of an observed rate.
challenges.answer: Disclosed that the WACC uses the marginal pre-tax cost of debt, quantified the observed-rate alternative at about four tenths of a point of WACC and four to five per cent of DCF value, and kept the house convention [S0][S2].

challenges.challenge: The 85% payout is not the level the board has paid, and it is not funded. The dividend record in the datapack is ex-date 10-Jun-2024 Rp35, 2-Jul-2025 Rp20, 7-May-2026 Rp50: the Rp35 is the FY2023 distribution (73.7% of FY2023 EPS of 47.49) and the FY2024 distribution was Rp20, which is 49.6% of FY2024 EPS of 40.33, not the 86.8% the assumptions claim. The three-year weighted payout is 72.8%, not 85%. More important, FY2026E dividends of Rp127.1bn plus capex of Rp60.2bn against LTM operating cash flow of Rp115.0bn cannot be funded as the assumptions describe, and net debt rises from Rp257.1bn to Rp309.1bn in FY2026E despite net_borrowing being set to zero.
challenges.answer: Re-mapped the dividend record by fiscal year (73.7, 49.6 and 88.6 per cent, three-year weighted 72.8), kept 85% with reasons between the average and the latest actual, and showed the dividend plus capex funded partly by the observed Rp36bn drawdown [S0][S4].

challenges.challenge: Section 6 says "insiders hold 96.9% and the free float is 11.3%", which is 108.2% of the register and cannot be true; the datapack carries insider_pct 96.947 and free_float_pct 11.26 with no reconciliation, and the report reproduces both without noticing. The free float is the input to the 30% constitutional haircut that produces the rating, so an unresolved 8.2pp contradiction in the register is not a footnote. Separately, neither section 5 nor section 6 mentions the one dated fact about the register: the float is below the IDX 15% minimum with 3.74pp to find by 2029-03-31, which is a known future supply event and the most likely trigger for the float widening section 5 speculates about.
challenges.answer: Removed the unreconciled insider figure and use only the IDX registry free float; added the below-minimum float and the compliance timetable running to 2029 as a supply risk and haircut catalyst [S0].

challenges.challenge: The report justifies not restating the fiscal-year history on the ground that "the company's investor site disallows automated collection in its robots file". The archived fund record (S12) allows the generic user agent - "User-agent: * / Allow: /" at lines 24-26 - and blocks only named AI crawlers including ClaudeBot and anthropic-ai; the corporate site is behind a CAPTCHA (S7), which is why the reader proxy failed. The stated reason is therefore inexact, and the more accurate statement is that no company document was obtainable within the tooling, which is a different and more serious limitation than a site policy.
challenges.answer: Corrected the reason: fund record allows the generic agent but disallows named AI crawlers, and the site is CAPTCHA-blocked; named both attempts and kept the evidence caveat in sections 3 and 6 [S12][S7].

challenges.challenge: Fact F20 (revenue_guidance) is stored as value 10.0 with scale 1 rather than 0.10 with scale 0.01, so the rendered report reads "which lands at the top of management's own 1000.0% growth range" in section 3. The underlying source says 5%-10% (S2). The model is unaffected but the published initiation prints a nonsense number in the paragraph that justifies the first key driver, and F21 and F22 use the correct convention.
challenges.answer: Rescaled F20 to 0.10 with scale 0.01 and checked every other pct fact for the same convention; the guidance now renders correctly [S2].

challenges.challenge: Section 4 closes: the probability-weighted value of Rp566 is -45.7% from the price before the liquidity adjustment. 566/730 - 1 is -22.5%; -45.7% is the post-haircut, pre-dividend return, so the sentence overstates the pre-haircut downside by 23pp in the paragraph that delivers the rating.
challenges.answer: The closing paragraph now separates the two numbers: the pre-haircut probability-weighted value is quoted against the price with no percentage attached, and the percentages that follow are labelled as the post-haircut price return and total return, which is what val.upside_pct and val.tr_pct actually measure. No clause claims a return for the pre-haircut value any more.

challenges.challenge: The EV/EBITDA cross-check carries 20% of the blend at Rp259 on 4.47x applied to a trailing EBITDA that still contains the pack Rp7.2bn depreciation - the figure the report says is wrong by an order of magnitude. Section 4 explains the -61.6% gap only as weak prior-year quarters.
challenges.answer: Dropped the EV/EBITDA leg from the blend rather than publish a peer multiple applied to a trailing EBITDA that carries the pack depreciation section three calls wrong. Section four states the metric the leg used, gives the company's own nine-month EBITDA-to-EBIT bridge as the evidence for the real charge, says a restated trailing metric would have pulled the blend down from the published value, and states the effect of the exclusion on the blend and the target.

challenges.challenge: F33 keys Gaikindo wholesales of 517,742 units as 9M2026. That is the January-July figure; AUTO F15 from the same source family has 679,020 units for 9M2026, so two names in one industry batch carry different values for the same series and period.
challenges.answer: F33 relabelled to 7M2026, which is what its own quote says (January-July 2026, from the S8 article dated 27 August). Added F40 for the January-September 2026 Gaikindo series of 679,020 units from the wartaekonomi report, and section two now uses the nine-month series for every comparison with BOLT so both sides cover the same period.

missing_bull_case.note: Three legs are missing. (1) The report never compares BOLT's margins or returns with the peers the house already rates BUY: a 22.9% nine-month gross margin against AUTO 15.6%, DRMA 17.4%, GJTL 18.9% and BRAM 16.5%, and a 16% ROE at the top of the group, is the evidence for the switching-cost moat section 2 argues, yet the terminal fade sets ROIC to exactly WACC and gives the spread zero value forever. The compounder card permits a moat-justified terminal ROIC above WACC; that option is never tested or priced. (2) Q3-2026 momentum is in the data and not in the bull: revenue +19.3% q/q and motorcycle parts Rp156bn, +28.5% q/q (S2), while the bull shocks annual growth only +3pp. (3) Section 5 quotes the bull at Rp890 (the scenario today-value) against a base of Rp819 (the 12-month target), so the upside case reads +8.7% when the like-for-like number is Rp941, +14.9%.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear omits the three risks the data actually shows. First, cash conversion has broken: LTM operating cash flow Rp115.0bn against LTM net profit Rp157.9bn (73%), Q3-2026 OCF -Rp5.0bn on record revenue, receivables Rp317.2bn vs Rp268.2bn at FY2025 (+18.2%) against LTM revenue +9.8% (1.86x, over the 1.5x divergence flag) and DSO 58.7 to 63.3 days. Second, the 85% payout is not funded: FY2026E dividends Rp127.1bn plus capex Rp60.2bn against LTM OCF Rp115.0bn, with net debt already up Rp36bn in nine months, and the FY2024 distribution was cut to Rp20 from Rp35. Third, the register has a dated supply event the report never mentions: free float 11.26% against the IDX 15% minimum, next step 2029-03-31 (3.74pp to find). The -30% y/y collapse in Q4-2025 revenue (Rp408.9bn vs Rp583.4bn) is dismissed as "the weak fourth quarter" without a cause, which is the one datum that would test the recovery-year thesis.

assumption_realism.note: The three value drivers do not all tie to their evidence. Revenue: the Q4-2026E leg is Rp460.8bn, 15% below Q3 and only +12.7% on a Q4-2025 base that was itself 30% below Q4-2024, while section 3 says the opposite; and the Q4 base of Rp408.9bn is attributed to S2, which does not contain it. Working capital: the 36.3% ratio is the datapack's nwc field (Rp665.0bn) but the report's own components (317.2 + 422.7 - 148.5) sum to Rp591.4bn, 32.3%. Payout: 85% rests on a mis-mapped FY2024 dividend; the record by fiscal year is 73.7%, 49.6%, 88.6%. Gross margin at 22.9% and opex at 10.2% are properly anchored on the nine months, and the capex budget is the company's own Rp60bn.

evidence_and_citations.note: The income statement is well evidenced: S2 and S4 are independent reports of the same keterbukaan informasi and their quotes match exactly, and the D&A derivation (Rp240bn EBITDA less Rp181bn EBIT) is sound arithmetic on a sourced bridge. Everything below the P&L is not. Net debt, minorities, associates, cash-flow history, receivables, inventory, payables and the whole dividend record come from S0, the Yahoo datapack, which has no archived text, and which the report itself proves wrong on D&A (7.2 vs ~59) and on capex. No company document exists: S7 is a 473-character CAPTCHA page and S12 is fund record, so the two-company-document standard is not met and the bridge carrying Rp495bn (29% of market cap) is unverified. Four of eleven sources are undated, including S6 (the acquisition) and S11 (the steel prices).

valuation_method_fit.note: The DCF is the right primary method, the stub, the 45.97% terminal share and the bridge (net debt 317.0 + minorities 169.9 - associates 7.9, all tied to the 30-Sep-2026 datapack) reconcile, and the implied exit multiple contracts (TV/EBITDA 5.2x, TV/EBIT 7.0x against 6.9x entry), so there is no multiple expansion wearing a DCF costume. The cross-checks are the problem: 15.16x P/E is the average of a 7.60x peer median and a ~22.7x own-history mean, and 9.99x EV/EBITDA the average of a 4.64x peer median and ~15.3x own history, so half the blend assumes a 33% P/E and 45% EV/EBITDA re-rating the report itself calls unearned. The discount rate is also not reproducible from the disclosed inputs, and no implied exit multiple is disclosed for the reader to run the multiple-survival test.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose says more than the evidence in two places and less in one. "Fairly priced and unownable at size" is a fair reading of Rp773 against Rp730, but the same section admits the reverse-DCF solver could not bracket the price and then converts that failure into a claim that "the market is pricing a slightly better business than we model" - an interpretation the failed solve does not support. Section 5's bear/bull/base comparison mixes today-values with a 12-month target and makes a mirrored scenario set look bearishly skewed. The rating itself is driven by one input, the Rp15.2m ADTV, which is constitutional and correctly applied but is a single unarchived aggregator field that moves the call from +13.2% to -13.3%.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: params is empty and the model reads no deck variable at all. Gaikindo and AISI volumes enter only through a hand-set growth path, which is defensible, but the macro deck's usd_idr FY2027E of 18,350 (against 18,103 spot) never touches the model although section 2 names the rupiah as one of three external influences and section 4 attributes the gross-margin drift to it; a 1.4% further depreciation on dollar-priced steel is asserted in prose and absent from the numbers. The desk's AVOID on rate-sensitive Indonesian consumer discretionary is consistent with REDUCE but is never cited, and the report does not reconcile its REDUCE with the house's BUY on AUTO, GJTL, SMSM, DRMA and BRAM at three to ten times earnings.

conservatism_audit.note: Below the last actual, the company's plan or the observed rate, without a source that forces it: the Q4-2026E revenue leg (Rp460.8bn, -15% q/q, unsourced and contradicted by the text); gross margin held at 22.9% against the FY2025 actual of 23.5%; capex ramped to 5.8% of sales in the terminal years against D&A of 4.15%, so capex exceeds depreciation by 40% forever; the terminal fade sets ROIC to exactly WACC, granting no perpetual moat value; and the WACC charges kd 9.45% while the P&L charges 6.8%, worth about 0.37pp of WACC and 4-5% of DCF value. None is quantified. The offsetting optimism is larger: a 33-45% multiple re-rating at half the blend weight, an 85% payout against a 73% record, and net borrowing set to zero while the dividend is in fact borrowed.

calibration.note: No BLOCK flags, but the gate reports a 4.09pp EBITDA-margin gap (FY2025A actual 12.76%, model 16.85%) and qc_justifications is empty. The gap is the D&A restatement itself: the model keeps the pack's FY2025A EBITDA of Rp212.7bn, which the report calls implausible, while the forecast uses 4.15% D&A, so FY2026E shows a 4.1pp margin jump that is pure restatement. The method card says wrong data is restated, not modelled around; one fact row (ebitda FY2025A = 205.5 + 4.15% x 1,666.6 = 274.7) would make the gate like-for-like and remove the non-comparable column the report apologises for in section 3.

signoff.notes: SELL earned: DCF Rp675, peer P/E Rp505 and blend Rp607 all sit below the Rp750 price before the 30% liquidity haircut, and dropping the EV/EBITDA leg raised the target, so the template issue works against the call, not for it. Batch bias check: the shared 11.9% WACC and 4.0% terminal growth are house defaults across the industry, and the static-multiple template defect is conservative here. Two FIX-level text errors should be corrected at publication: section 4 says a one-point WACC move is about 7% when the adjacent grid shows -13%/+17%, and section 3 calls 10.0% model profit growth close to the 15.0% management guide. Neither changes the target.

bias.note: FY2026E revenue is the top of management 5-10% guidance and a Q4 at the prior-year level is exactly what that 10% implies, so it is the plan, not a haircut; gross margin is held at the observed 22.9% [S2]. The conservative departures are disclosed and quantified: the WACC charges a 9.45% marginal cost of debt against the 6.5-6.8% actually paid (about 4-5% of DCF, section 4) and terminal capex ramps to 5.8%. Dropping the EV/EBITDA leg raises the blended value from about Rp553 to Rp607 and the target by about Rp44, so the exclusion weakens the SELL rather than protecting it. findings.finding: weights.changed is the only engine flag and assumptions qc_justifications is empty. Section 4 argues the EV/EBITDA exclusion, and the argument is sound on its own terms: a restated leg at about Rp392 (4.47x on LTM EBITDA of about Rp316bn) would cut the blend to about Rp553 and the target to about Rp406, so dropping it raises the target and weakens the call. What is not argued is why the survivors are 0.6/0.4 rather than the 0.625/0.375 renormalisation of the industry default 0.5/0.3/0.2, and no justification is recorded. Section 4 also says restating the trailing metric needs the audited annual statements, which is not correct: LTM EBITDA is constructible as LTM EBIT plus the same 4.15% D&A ratio the forecast already uses, from the reported 9M EBITDA of Rp240bn less EBIT of Rp181bn [S2].

FY2024A and FY2025A EBITDA still print the data pack figures of Rp187.5bn and Rp212.7bn on depreciation of Rp6.8bn and Rp7.2bn. On the report own 4.15% basis they are about Rp251bn and Rp275bn, margins of 14.8% and 16.5% against FY2026E of 16.85%. That is why the calibration gate fires a 4.09pp gap: the like-for-like gap is about 0.3pp, so the flag is a data artefact, but the model still prints a 45% FY2026E EBITDA jump and the gate will fire on every future version. The round-1 Q4 FIX was closed by disclosure only.

Section 3 still says FY2026E attributable profit of Rp145.4bn is close to the 15.0% growth management guides to. The model grows attributable profit 10.0% (132.2 to 145.4); group profit is up about 18% before the 12% minority. Round-1 Q5 left this open and close to overstates the alignment by five points in the paragraph that justifies the first key driver [S2][S6].

Section 4 says a one-point move in the WACC moves the DCF value by roughly seven per cent; the adjacent grid gives Rp675 to Rp586 (-13%) at +1pp and Rp789 (+17%) at -1pp, and 7% is the half-point move. Terminal growth at +1pp is +9.2%. The sensitivity ranking in the same paragraph is correct on the fresh grid (two points of growth is about 5.5%).
Section 6 dates the IDX-IC free-float mirror 27 October 2026; the datapack registry entry is dated 2026-11-04 [S0].

The P/E leg applies the 8.38x peer median to LTM attributable profit of Rp141.2bn (FY2025 132.2 less 9M2025 107.8 plus 9M2026 116.7) while the text compares BOLT 12.1x FY2026E with the peers 8.4x trailing. The mixed basis makes the premium look about 3% smaller than it is, marginally bearish.
